rounds.fact: Ask Jeeves branded itself around a friendly butler mascot and the pitch of asking questions in plain English, a contrast to the keyword-heavy search engines of the era.
Amazon started as an online bookstore in 1994. By 1999 the homepage was already a dense grid of categories and personalized recommendations, a layout philosophy it never really abandoned.
Webshots was one of the most popular photo-sharing communities of the early 2000s, and was also widely used as a source for desktop wallpaper downloads.
Engadget launched in 2004 and quickly became one of the most-read gadget blogs, known for live-blogging tech keynotes years before that became a standard practice across tech media.
Tucows started in 1993 as a curated shareware download library (the name stood for 'The Ultimate Collection of Winsock Software') before evolving into an internet services company.
